risks.risk: Foreign currency risk concentrated in USD
risks.note: Company operates globally and is exposed to foreign exchange risk; around 70% to 90% of its foreign currency exposure is in USD. Every one percentage point depreciation/appreciation in the exchange rate between the Indian rupee and foreign currencies would affect profit-before-tax margin by approximately 0.21%. Mitigated via plain-vanilla forward contracts designated as cash flow hedges against expected USD receivables, governed by Board-approved hedging policy.

Trade receivables are typically unsecured and are derived from revenue earned from customers primarily located in the United States, concentrating credit risk in a single geography/customer base. Managed by a dedicated Credit Task Force through credit approvals and credit-limit monitoring.

Receivables overdue for more than 180 days stood at ₹858.83 Million as at March 31, 2026 (2.6% of total receivables of ₹32,746.57 Million), of which ₹332.74 Million has been provided for; credit risk is assessed using an expected-credit-loss model under Ind AS 109.

Company's investments in mutual funds expose it to NAV-driven price risk; a 5% NAV move would affect the mutual-fund investment value by ₹608.07 Million as at March 31, 2026 (₹310.61 Million a year earlier), managed through portfolio diversification.

Company identifies liquidity risk as one of the three principal categories of financial risk it is exposed to, alongside market risk and credit risk, overseen by the Risk Management Committee, though no further quantification is given in this bundle.

one-line thesis: Persistent used this Sunday call to announce two transformational moves at once: (1) a net-new large deal — ~$125m+ annual ACV, ~$650m+ over 6.5 years — with an existing US-HQ global tech customer, accretive to revenue & margin from Q2 and extending the 24-quarter growth streak; and (2) an all-cash acquisition of Germany's Nagarro at €1.27bn EV (€81/share, 140% premium) to form a $2.9bn+, 46,000-person "AI-led digital engineering powerhouse" — the 2nd-largest digital-engineering player globally. The deal vaults Europe from ~8% to 22% of revenue, adds ERP/CX/Public-Sector and OpenAI/SAP franchises, and puts the $5bn-by-FY31 aspiration within reach. The bet: Persistent's growth rigor (23.9% 5-yr CAGR) can revive a flat, margin-pressured Nagarro (2 years flat, stock −85% from peak); the risk: a debt-funded (1.9–2.5x levered) integration of an asset roughly two-thirds Persistent's size.
financial scorecard (deal + standalone m: > One-offs / distortions: transaction expenses hit Year-1 reported P&L (stripped out, EPS still accretive). Goodwill/intangibles ~70/30; intangibles amortized over 8 years. Nagarro's FCF ~2x PAT (interest below the line).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Large deal ramp: ~$125m+ ACV, ~$650m+ over 6.5 years; net-new (may involve employee transitions, minimal ramp); revenue & margin accretive from Q2 onward; margins "fairly healthy" (below company average but healthy). "Cements the growth for Persistent for this year."

Combined growth: confident of sustaining Persistent's growth momentum; intent to bring Nagarro back to "industry-leading growth" (in a European context). No combined numeric growth guide given (transaction pending regulatory approval).

Margins: combined entity "not at any significant lower margins than Persistent today"; cost synergies exist but will be reinvested into growth; confident of maintaining and bettering margins over time; lifting Nagarro's EBIT via integration/synergy plans.
$5bn revenue by FY31 aspiration — deal gets them there "at a nice scale"; Europe to 15%+ (combination lands 22%).
EPS: Cash EPS accretive Year 1; Reported EPS accretive Year 1 (ex one-time transaction costs).
Leverage: Net debt / combined EBITDA 1.9x–2.5x (depends on open-offer acceptance) → target ~1.0x by FY2030.
No QIP / no equity dilution intended; may bring PE at the asset (Nagarro) level later to deleverage. Value-creation / revenue-cost synergy plan to be detailed post regulatory approvals.
order book & pipeline: Large deal is the marquee item — net-new, end-to-end product engineering + product support for "a significant portfolio of products globally" for an existing US tech-leader customer (name under NDA). Won partly on the AI "do more for less / far more for same" pitch.

Cross-sell / mining runway: >350 combined accounts >$1m; ~180 Nagarro logos >$1m with top client <$50m — "don't need to hunt for new logos," mine existing. Single-digit customer overlap (<10 accounts, in different org parts).
Persistent account maturation: top-4 customers now avg >$100m; two accounts >$100m, third nearing.
segment / subsidiary detail (nagarro pro: Geography: Nagarro Europe-heavy (35% NA); adds scaled nearshore Europe delivery (Germany, Italy, France, Switzerland, Spain, Turkey), plus Middle East, Japan, Israel entry where Persistent is minimal.

Verticals: strong in Industrial & Consumer, fledgling Public Sector; automotive is a small part (more digital-side, so auto slowdown low-impact); travel/transportation. Complementary to Persistent's TMT/BFSI/HLS.

Clients/partnerships: Siemens (product engineering + GTM), Lufthansa, SAP (key implementation partner + product engineering), OpenAI (one of few accredited resellers + forward-deployed engineering practice). Persistent brings Anthropic + hyperscaler partnerships + its SASVA AI engineering platform/IP.
Culture/integration: Nagarro already India-heavy (13,500 of 18,500 in India) → mgmt argues an easier India-Europe integration than a pure onshore-European target ("takes one big thorn out").
growth verticals / optionality: ERP (via Nagarro/SAP) + CX (Persistent) → end-to-end transformation capability Persistent lacked at scale.
OpenAI reseller + forward-deployed AI engineering franchise; combined AI capability "possibly much bigger than any similarly-sized general-purpose IT player."
Nearshore Europe + Middle East + Japan + Israel + embedded-software practice — new addressable markets.
Positions the group as 2nd-largest digital-engineering player globally, 7th-largest India-listed tech-services company.
margins & cost dynamics: Cost synergies acknowledged but explicitly to be redeployed into growth, not dropped to margin.
Nagarro margin uplift thesis: recently-hired professional CFO (Prateek Aggarwal) tightening a previously loosely-run finance org; integration/synergy plans to raise EBIT.

AI/T&M cannibalization: Persistent already cannibalizes its own T&M revenue via AI tooling + own IP (SASVA); T&M model "not dead for the next few years" but "increasingly goes down." Strategy = win disproportionately by moving the AI capability needle faster than larger peers.
Cash: both firms strong cash generators; intent to service/repay the acquisition debt from operating cash; shift from CapEx to OpEx working-capital funding.
capex / expansion — deal financing & str: Structure: acquire 100% of Nagarro, EV €1.27bn (€81/share cash) = equity €1bn (12.4m shares ex-treasury) + net debt €267m. EV/Revenue 1.27x, EV/EBITDA 9.12x (drops to 7.73x on upper-end CY26 guidance). Premium 140% to undisturbed close (25–26 Jun) / 94% to 3-mo VWAP.

Stakes: already secured 21% via SPA from the major shareholder; management board (~13–14%) to tender → ~35%; "35–40% more or less committed." Minimum acceptance 50%+1 share (voluntary public takeover offer under German law); aim for as close to 100% as possible.

Financing: fully via committed bridge from Barclays; rate Euribor + 175–250bps ≈ 4.1–4.8%; total facility €1.4bn (incl. refinancing Nagarro debt); PSL provides €1.4bn corporate guarantee. No QIP, no equity dilution.

Timeline: offer announced 26-Jun-2026 → BaFin filing within ~4 weeks → ~10 working days–2 weeks clearance → 4-week acceptance (+optional 2 weeks) → Persistent AGM last week of July to seek shareholder approval → expected close towards Q4 CY2026 / early Q1 CY2027. RBI + multi-country regulatory approvals required.

Post-close: no Domination/Profit-Loss-Transfer Agreement (DPLTA) for 2 years; run Nagarro with its management, then squeeze out minorities at the right time ("no hurry"). Becomes one entity eventually.
capital allocation: All-cash, all-debt acquisition — deliberately no equity dilution/QIP; may introduce PE at the asset level later to deleverage. Confident combined EBITDA + cash generation services the debt; leverage 1.9–2.5x → ~1x by FY2030.
Rationale: "not about buying cheap, but buying the right asset" — control transaction, complementary, compare to private control transactions not just listed peer multiples.
risks & watch-items: Turnaround risk: Nagarro flat ~2 yrs, stock −85% from ~€212 peak; margin pressure; horizontal-tech/energy-utilities/telecom/travel verticals saw sharp declines. Recovery hinges on Persistent's integration + GTM rigor.
Integration / two-year run-as-independent (no DPLTA for 2 yrs) — growth-engine continuity risk on an asset ~two-thirds Persistent's size (analysts pressed hard on this).
Leverage / interest cost: €1.4bn debt at ~4.1–4.8%; ~$41m interest cost cited by an analyst; repayment depends on cash generation + open-offer acceptance %.
Acceptance uncertainty: deal conditional on 50%+1 share; scenario risk if acceptance falls short.
AI deflation of T&M (68% of Nagarro revenue is T&M) — structural revenue-cannibalization headwind industry-wide.
BaFin queries on Nagarro's books (Allgeier carve-out era + accounting principles) — mgmt says diligence done, no performance impact; still a governance watch-item.
Long-tail small accounts / smaller average deal size at Nagarro vs Persistent's scaled clients — possible tail-account rationalization (frees SG&A).
management quality / tone: Confident, well-rehearsed, founder-led (Anand Deshpande opened; Kalra dialed in from Munich). Strong strategic articulation of complementarity ("not a consolidation play, an expansion play"; "partnership made in heaven"). CFO Vinit Teredesai crisp on deal mechanics.

Handled skeptical questions directly — corrected an analyst's "high single digit" EBIT claim with exact figures (CY25 10.9%, Q1CY26 12.1%), acknowledged flat Nagarro revenue and integration risk without over-promising, deferred the detailed value-creation plan to post-approval ("won't jump the gun"). Repeatedly leaned on Persistent's own track record as the credibility anchor. Tone: ambitious but measured on synergy specifics (appropriately, given pending approvals).
non-obvious takeaways: This is a scaled Europe M&A that Persistent had flagged as its stated strategy for years — chosen over an onshore-European target specifically because Nagarro is already India-heavy (13,500/18,500 in India), lowering integration risk.
The large deal is arguably the more certain value driver than the acquisition: net-new, ~$650m/6.5yr, margin-accretive from Q2, and it "cements" FY27 growth independent of Nagarro's turnaround.

Deal is all-cash, all-debt by design — management explicitly rejected a share-swap (public-to-private German mechanics differ from PE deals) and ruled out any QIP; deleveraging optionality parked at the asset level (inbound PE interest already, within 24 hrs).

Nagarro's 68% T&M mix is framed not as a risk but as consistent with the "build-side" engineering model (vs larger peers' support/managed-services T&M) — the AI-cannibalization exposure is acknowledged but positioned as an offensive lever ("win more while cannibalizing").
The $5bn-by-FY31 ambition, previously questioned on whether Persistent needed more verticals, is answered by this deal (adds Industrial/Consumer/Public-Sector + ERP + nearshore Europe in one stroke).

Combined $2.9bn+, 46,000+ staff, 40+ countries; Europe 8%→22%; NA 81%→62%. Bridge financing €1.4bn from Barclays (~4.1–4.8%), leverage 1.9–2.5x → ~1x by FY2030; no QIP. Cash + reported EPS accretive Year 1 (ex one-offs). Min acceptance 50%+1; 21% secured, ~35–40% committed. Close ~Q4 CY26 / early Q1 CY27; AGM last week of July. Persistent standalone: FY26 rev $1.654bn, 5-yr CAGR 23.9%, op margin ~15.6%, PAT margin ~12.6%. $5bn-by-FY31 aspiration reaffirmed.

Next Q → check: (1) open-offer acceptance % (50%+1 threshold; path to ~100%); (2) BaFin/RBI/multi-country approvals + close timing (Q4CY26/Q1CY27); (3) AGM approval (late July); (4) large-deal revenue actually flowing from Q2 + margin impact; (5) Nagarro margin trajectory (EBIT 12.1% → up?) and revenue de-flattening; (6) net-debt/EBITDA vs 1.9–2.5x guide + deleverage path; (7) any PE participation at Nagarro asset level; (8) combined-group growth guide once value-creation plan is published post-approval.

Leverage / interest cost: €1.4bn debt at ~4.1–4.8%; ~$41m interest cost cited by an analyst; repayment depends on cash generation + open-offer acceptance %.
Acceptance uncertainty: deal conditional on 50%+1 share; scenario risk if acceptance falls short.
AI deflation of T&M (68% of Nagarro revenue is T&M) — structural revenue-cannibalization headwind industry-wide.
BaFin queries on Nagarro's books (Allgeier carve-out era + accounting principles) — mgmt says diligence done, no performance impact; still a governance watch-item.
Long-tail small accounts / smaller average deal size at Nagarro vs Persistent's scaled clients — possible tail-account rationalization (frees SG&A).
management quality / tone: Confident, well-rehearsed, founder-led (Anand Deshpande opened; Kalra dialed in from Munich). Strong strategic articulation of complementarity ("not a consolidation play, an expansion play"; "partnership made in heaven"). CFO Vinit Teredesai crisp on deal mechanics.

Handled skeptical questions directly — corrected an analyst's "high single digit" EBIT claim with exact figures (CY25 10.9%, Q1CY26 12.1%), acknowledged flat Nagarro revenue and integration risk without over-promising, deferred the detailed value-creation plan to post-approval ("won't jump the gun"). Repeatedly leaned on Persistent's own track record as the credibility anchor. Tone: ambitious but measured on synergy specifics (appropriately, given pending approvals).
non-obvious takeaways: This is a scaled Europe M&A that Persistent had flagged as its stated strategy for years — chosen over an onshore-European target specifically because Nagarro is already India-heavy (13,500/18,500 in India), lowering integration risk.
The large deal is arguably the more certain value driver than the acquisition: net-new, ~$650m/6.5yr, margin-accretive from Q2, and it "cements" FY27 growth independent of Nagarro's turnaround.

Deal is all-cash, all-debt by design — management explicitly rejected a share-swap (public-to-private German mechanics differ from PE deals) and ruled out any QIP; deleveraging optionality parked at the asset level (inbound PE interest already, within 24 hrs).

Nagarro's 68% T&M mix is framed not as a risk but as consistent with the "build-side" engineering model (vs larger peers' support/managed-services T&M) — the AI-cannibalization exposure is acknowledged but positioned as an offensive lever ("win more while cannibalizing").
The $5bn-by-FY31 ambition, previously questioned on whether Persistent needed more verticals, is answered by this deal (adds Industrial/Consumer/Public-Sector + ERP + nearshore Europe in one stroke).

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
